pr_title: Hook up the keybindings to the SUI, redux
pr_body:
## Summary of the Pull Request

This is a redux of #8882. 

From the original:

>  This is really similar to what we're doing with the `CommandPalette`. We're adding a ~~Preview~~`KeyDown` handler to the SUI `MainPage`, that connects to `TerminalPage::_HandleKey`. That allows the SUI a chance to search the keymap to dispatch actions for keybindings, similar to how the command palette does it. 
> 
> This also means it's now possible for the SUI to invoke _all_ the actions available to the Terminal. This includes the ones like `IncreaseFontSize`, which require a _Terminal_ to actually do something. So we have to make sure all the calls to `_GetActiveControl` actually check that the result is non-null before using it. 
> 
> A bunch of the actions do nothing now from a SUI tab, others behave _weird_. Like "Rename tab" / "Open Tab Renamer" do nothing. "Duplicate Tab" again does nothing - we try making a new settings tab, which just focuses the settings tab again. "Copy text" definitely does nothing, same with paste.

I don't know why I thought this wouldn't work. I thought we'd have to do this in `PreviewKeyDown` or something, which led to [weirdness](https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/pull/8882#issuecomment-767088554). Turns out, we don't need it to be in `PreviewKeyDown`. It can just be in the SUI's `KeyDown`.

## References
* Original: #8882
* Workaround was in #8885


## PR Checklist
* [x] Closes #8767
* [x] I work here
* [x] Tests added/passed
* [n/a] Requires documentation to be updated

## Detailed Description of the Pull Request / Additional comments

The special case handler from #8885 is no longer needed

## Validation Steps Performed

* Switching tabs with Ctrl+Tab works
* Command palette works
* fullscreen, focus mode works
* close window works
* copy paste on Ctrl+C/V works, even when bound
* Select all text in textboxes works
* tab navigation through UI elements works

issue_context.title: Make SettingsTab respect keybindings
issue_context.body:
# Description of the new feature/enhancement

Some keybindings should be respected when in the settings tab. At the very least, we should respect "closeTab".

Ideally, we'd respect all app-level keybindings. This includes tab management, mode switching (i.e always on top, focus mode, fullscreen, etc...), and command palette. In the end, we'll really have "support" for "all" keybindings because the architecture checks if there's a terminal that can actually handle the action.
comments:
> @carlos-zamora - does tab-switcher works for you when you attempt to start from the settings tab? As it doesn't for me - I am stuck there and cannot escape 😄
> 
> I mean literally cannot escape - is there a way to leave the settings tab with a keyboard?
> 
> Update: I succeeded to escape, by focusing the tab view item 😊 Wondering why the key event doesn't propagate to the terminal page..

The short version for why it doesn't work is because we handle keybindings pretty weird. When we create a `TermControl`, we pass in the keybindings (via `TerminalSettings`). From there, we detect keystrokes and go back to TermApp to actually do the action.

So basically, we need to pass these keybindings over to the Settings UI and detect them there. But then we get into another problem, not all keybindings should be valid (i.e. copy/paste shouldn't be valid). I think CommandPalette got around this issue by specifically detecting only a few of them?

Long-term, a refactor of our actions model needs to be done. Half of that refactor is being able to identify where a defined action came from (defaults.json vs settings.json). The other half (more relevant to this discussion) is figuring out a better way to detect keybindings. We still get some weird behavior like not being able to detect keybindings in a search box.

@carlos-zamora - we recently added keybinding handling to the TerminalPage - see the key-down handler there. So I would expect the routed event to propagate there if not handled by the settings tab. 

For instance this is how it works when you issue a chord in the command palette or when focused on the searchbox. 

The terminal control is a special case because we wanted to reverse the order of handling (I am still not sure why preview key down in the TerminalPage won't do the job).

However here I hoped it will work the same. But something seems to swallow the events.

Here's my thought though - like _real long term_, I want to be able to have panes that don't host terminals in them. So _eventually_, we'll want this work to be done. Might as well do it now. 

Plus, we definitely want `SwitchToTab`, but also probably `NewTab`, `CloseTab`... I'm not sure if that's it or now. May as well just go for it and do 'em all.

Oh, we can't have the copy and paste keybindings that you've set for the Terminal work in the SUI, because of the way those keybindings are handled. >  Terminal was a UWP app as opposed to a traditional .exe like vscode and others are. 

That's not strictly true - it doesn't really make sense to think about apps as Win32 vs UWP apps anymore. The Terminal actually is a traditional exe, that just so happens to be using UWP XAML for its UI. Nowadays, win32 applications have access to basically the whole gamut of UWP APIs, so the line between the two is blurrier and blurrier.

> I've noticed in Terminal, Settings and Feedback Hub, you cannot drag the size of sidebar. Is that something that is hard defined in the UWP design language or can that be implemented on an app-by-app basis?

I believe that's just a hardcoded part of the `NavigationView` in WinUI.

> Lastly (and out of scope of terminal), is there a way to give feedback to MSFT about the Settings app in general and asking them to not get rid of Control Panel in a future update? (I don't know if they were planning on removing it in favor of Settings UWP completely.)

Frankly, I don't really know. Every team happens to have their own ways of doing things. Typically the Feedback hub is a good place to start. I don't know if UserVoice is still a thing, but I know we used that before we moved to being entirely on GitHub.
